findings.title: R2-04: Local cancellation normal form and noncrossing ancestry for Rule 30
findings.claim: Every output disagreement admits a factorization preserving its leftmost differing parent with even remaining contributions. For any two Rule 30 histories, every surviving disagreement has an initial disagreement ancestor and root labels are spatially nondecreasing at every finite time; this is specialized to the official single-seed histories.
findings.scope: All six Boolean local inputs; arbitrary Rule 30 histories on the integer line, all natural times. The official seed specialization allows all T,P,t. Literal path involutions are finite-tested only: T=0..3, P=1..4, through time 10.
findings.result: Unchanged official checker passed all 44 custom declarations and 12 headlines. Exact finite involutions preserved zero/one residuals, including even path families through zero-disagreement vertices. No center survivor is asserted.

findings.title: R2-04: The least-source frontier retreats; monotone progress is false
findings.claim: The candidate strengthening R_(t+1)>=R_t for the rightmost descendant of the least initial disagreement is false, already for canonical Rule30 T=P=1 at t=1 to t=2.
findings.scope: Finite physical/packed witness: root descendants {-3,-1} at t=1 become {-4,-2} at t=2. A separate open sufficient conjecture asks for some center reach for every T>=0,P>=1.
findings.result: The witness agrees under physical truth-table evolution, selected-parent propagation, and packed masks. The weaker center-reach conjecture survived 4096 rectangular plus 32 held-out comparisons through 4*(T+P)+128, but has no unbounded proof.

findings.title: R2-03: bounded rank cannot satisfy the original three-observation descent guard
findings.claim: The proposed replacement score R(T,P) in 0..B, strictly decreasing under two steps whenever three canonical center observations agree, cannot exist universally.
findings.scope: Every uniformly bounded natural score on canonical pairs, including ranks of all fixed-dimensional matrices over any field. Not the unbounded integer off-diagonal score from round one.
findings.result: A written pigeonhole proof forces B+1 strict drops; exact single-seed witnesses cover B=1,2,3. At B=2, T=1,P=25 gives the repeated block 1011100.

findings.title: R2-03: nonlinear source parities at separated binary scales
findings.claim: The dyadic difference matrix M(T,n,K)[i,j]=c(T+i+2^(K+j))+c(T+i), with 2^K>T+n-1 over GF(2), has an exact nonlinear source representation. Unbounded rank for T=0 would imply official Problem 1.
findings.scope: Actual Rule 30 single-seed center, with explicit finite-support and binary-kernel conditions. Proposed sufficient growth lemma U is open.
findings.result: Known Duhamel decomposition specialized to separated binary scales; 760 exact block checks and 32,780 crosschecked bits. Tested square-family ranks through size 12 are 0,1,1,3,5,6,6,7,8,10,10,11. Eventual period P after T0 bounds every such rank by T0+P.

findings.title: R2-03: time-monotone rank and a near-full-rank shortcut fail
findings.claim: Two proposed strengthenings fail: nondecreasing rank as T advances, and rank M(0,n,ceil(log2 n)) >= n-1 for every n>=2.
findings.scope: Actual single-seed center with the admissible separation condition. These failures concern only the two strengthenings, not the open growth lemma.
findings.result: At n=2,K=8, T=0 to T=1 drops rank 1 to 0. At n=3,K=2, rows 000,001,000 have rank 1, below n-1=2.

findings.title: R2-01: the generic barrier's two-step witnesses are satisfied by background-retaining and by resynchronizing readers
findings.claim: With A, M, Z the barrier's startWord/middleWord/endWord, an 8-state prefix-match reader (cost 1 per letter matching the phase background (1100001)^inf for A,Z and (1011111)^inf for M; reject sink otherwise) satisfies all three conditions of no_absorbing_prefix_geometric_rank for every integer lambda>=1 with nonnegative 0/1 costs (B = H1 on every word); sliding-window readers W_L (cost 1 when the last L+1 letters are a background factor) satisfy them at lambda=1 for L=5..15 and for every lambda>=1 for L=8..15.
findings.scope: Exactly the barrier's three conditions on its three explicit words; kit ZBL convention; prefix reader is not absorbed on commonWord, W_L never absorbs. Not the full rank requirement.
findings.result: Exact integer computation: prefix-match lengths A/M/Z = 30/28/26 with Z's matched positions a strict subset of A's; H1=0, H0=E1(Z)-E0(M) works. These energies are NOT ranks; they only show that the barrier's witness set cannot be reused against these classes.

findings.title: R2-01: unit-scale definite (resynchronizing) readers reduce to Rule 30^4 conservation laws; none exist for window m<=11
findings.claim: Paper reduction: if a definite reader with delay L (energy H_r + sum phi_r(last L+1 letters), lambda=1, signed rational costs) satisfies drop-by-1 on free-zero steps and non-increase on free-one steps for every guarded row (ether-phase prefix + arbitrary tail, both phases) and E_1 is bounded below, then phi_1 is a conserved density of four Rule 30 steps; if that density is trivial, E_r = H_r + c|w| + O(1) with c>=0 and a long truncated ether orbit contradicts the required drops. Computation: Rule 30^k (k=1,2,4) has only trivial conserved densities of window m<=10, and Rule 30^4 for m=11.
findings.scope: Unit scale only; definite readers only; rows inside the barrier's Safe13 0101/1010 domains; the full rank requirement on those rows (stronger than the barrier's two steps).
findings.result: Exact: GF(2^31-1) rank of the conservation system reaches the trivial upper bound 2^(m-1) for all 31 Rule 30 cases (m<=10 for k=1,2,4; m=11 for k=4), which certifies over Q that only trivial laws exist; Rule 184 control shows the expected one-dimensional extra law. Hence, with the (unformalized) reduction, no unit-scale definite reader with L<=10 supplies the rank. Truncated ether rows stay guarded ~ (l-27)/2 double steps (109 at l=240).

findings.title: R2-01: readers that absorb only off finitely many backgrounds (incl. the round-two 1,110-state union reader) admit no unit-scale rank on the Golden-guarded domain
findings.claim: For any reader T with sink s that is absorbed on (P) pump rows next(Q ++ 0^30 ++ Y'^n ++ 1) and their successors (Q a 40-cell ether-phase prefix, Y in {0,1,10000000}) and (X) on Theta(g)[1..78] within p0 cells for every length-40 factor g of the Fibonacci Golden stream f (A->01, B->011): there is no unit-scale two-phase signed rank (drop on free zero, non-increase on free one, every Golden-13-guarded row with actual finite past; E_1 bounded below).
findings.scope: lambda=1; same T for both phases; previous-bit phases; step domain = Golden-guarded rows (wider than the barrier's 0101 lower-bound domain). The 1,110-state reader satisfies (P) for n<=40 and (X) exhaustively with p0=16.
findings.result: Exact checks: pump slopes give six inequalities; an exact Fraction certificate forces C1(s,0)=C1(s,1)=C0(s,0)=C0(s,1)=a, a>=0 by the white pump; along the Fibonacci orbit (W=801, 360 double steps, 151 free zeros, guard ok, prefix = Theta(shift^j f)) the reader sinks within 16 cells, so E = a*length + O(1) cannot fall by the unbounded number of zeros. Consistent with the archived unit-scale alpha=0 optima, which used richer models not covered here.

findings.title: Left-edge agreement depth depends only on v2(p) and is constant in t for v2(p)<=3: the constants are 8, 29, 400
findings.claim: In the moving integer frame from the single-cell seed, depth(t,p), the number of leading left-edge cells on which row t and row t-p agree, was identical for every tested p of the same 2-adic valuation and identical for every t in [3000,6000): 8 at v2=1, 29 at v2=2, 400 at v2=3. At v2(p)>=4 it is not constant in t. The 29-cell period-4 prefix independently corroborates the 26-cell common ether prefix assumed by the kernel-checked absorbing-prefix barrier, so that barrier hypothesis is generic on this orbit rather than a corner case.
findings.scope: Single black cell seed; Phi(a)=a XOR ((a<<1)|(a<<2)); rows high-bit aligned; T=6000; every t in [3000,6000); p in {2,6,10,14,4,12,20,28,36,44,8,24,40,56,72,16,48,80,32,96}. Pure enumeration.
findings.result: Ran. Constants reproduce exactly across all tested p within each valuation class and all t in range.

verification.limits: T=6000 rows; t restricted to [3000,6000); 20 periods; single seed; Python ints, no solver, no timeout reached; runtime under 5 minutes on one core.

findings.title: Sharp transition at v2(p)=4: the regular region goes from a bounded strip to a constant fraction (about 0.375) of the light cone
findings.claim: For v2(p)<=3 the agreement depth is a constant and its share of the cone (2t+1) tends to zero. For v2(p)>=4 the depth grows linearly in t, holding a fraction near 0.375 across t=1000 to t=7999, an eightfold range. At p=16 the fraction read 0.385, 0.377, 0.381, 0.378, 0.376. Therefore roughly three eighths of every row lies in a period-16 regular region that begins beyond the 29-cell strip, entirely outside what a prefix reader absorbing on the ether prefix can observe.
findings.result: Ran. Fraction stable near 0.375 for v2>=4; p=8 control pinned at exactly 400 at t=1000, 4000 and 7999.

verification.limits: T=8000 rows; five t values; six periods; no solver; runtime under 5 minutes on one core.

findings.title: Proposed well-founded resource: Dershowitz-Manna multiset over non-regular blocks, with the period-16 regular region as the identity element
findings.claim: Proposal, not run. Take the F002 period-16 regular region as the identity, decompose the complement into maximal non-regular blocks, and order the finite multiset of blocks by Dershowitz-Manna under a per-block ordinal. This is not of the barred form: a DM multiset order is not a signed integer prefix energy with geometric per-letter costs, and the regular region is an identity element rather than an absorbing reader state. Ether insertion and long vacuum segments are rank-invariant by construction, and block mergers are safe because DM permits removing an element. MISSING LEMMA, stated exactly: for every Rule 30 step in which one non-regular block splits into two or more, each child is strictly below the parent in the chosen per-block ordinal. Splits are the only direction DM does not give for free.
findings.scope: Mechanism shape only. No per-block ordinal is defined, so no proof obligation is discharged.

findings.title: R2-07: two finite right halves refute the C=2 critical charge, for every additive allowance B
findings.claim: With the official definitions, CriticalCharge C B R := forall n, 5*zeros (free R) n <= n + B + C*blackCount (Psi R) (2*n+1), there are finite right halves whose ratio (5*zeros(free R,n) - n)/blackCount(Psi R,2*n+1) exceeds 2, so CriticalCharge 2 B R is false for every B. W1 has black cells exactly at positions 3, 7, 11 and ratio tending to 21/10; W2 has black cells exactly at positions 4, 5, 6, 9, 13, 16, 17, 18 and ratio about 2.3288. This extends the published C=1 refutation one coefficient further: the smallest natural coefficient not refuted by anything tested here is 3.
findings.scope: Official coordinates and definitions at research base 102d5b8e: rule a b c = xor a (b || c); altCol t = (t % 2 == 0); drv as in Rule30Ether; u R s = drv altCol R (2*s+1) 1; Psi R = Theta (fun s => !u R s); free R k = zrow (Psi R) (2*k+1) 1; zeros and blackCount as in Rule30CriticalChargeOneCoreResearch, so blackCount (Psi R) (2*n+1) counts depths 0..2*n. Finite computation to n = 20000, i.e. depths 0..40000, in exact integer arithmetic. Right halves are finite: white at every position beyond the listed support.
findings.result: Observed exactly. For W1 the free stream is the alternating stream with a single phase slip at index 2 at every one of 20000 steps, Psi W1 is exactly period 14 with 5 black per period from depth 100 to depth 40000, and 5*zeros-n-2*blackCount takes the values 28, 138, 350, 708, 1422 at n = 500, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000, which is linear growth, so no additive B absorbs it. For W2 the same quantity takes 55, 375, 1019, 2091, 4233. On every witness 5*zeros-n-3*blackCount is negative and decreasing. Before any of this the same code reproduces the published kernel-checked C=1 witness exactly: free stream 0101..., sideways row 1100001 repeated, zeros = 7k and blackCount = 12k at n = 14k, ratio 7/4, and the packed word matches the brief's 0x6b70. A separately written non-bit-packed implementation agrees cell for cell. NOT proved: that the free streams continue past n = 20000.

verification.limits: Exact integer arithmetic, no floating point, no solver, no Lean, standard library only. The simulated width always exceeds the true support, which spreads rightwards at speed one, so the truncation is exact rather than approximate. Horizon n = 20000 and depths 0..40000. This is NOT a kernel replay and no checker was run. A 20000-step agreement is not an infinite assertion.

findings.title: R2-07: both sides of the charge depend only on the free stream, and a transient rather than the periodic part buys the excess
findings.claim: Because Psi R = Theta (free R) and free R k = zrow (Psi R) (2*k+1) 1, both sides of the critical charge are functionals of the single stream f = free R; the right half enters only by deciding which streams are achievable. Since free R is always Golden, the excess 5*zeros(f,n)-n grows at a rate of at most 3/2, attained exactly on the eventually alternating streams, so the smallest uniform constant the charge could use is sup_f (3/2)/(2*density of Theta f) over those streams. Measured: purely periodic Golden streams never exceed ratio 7/4, every ratio above 2 comes from a transient, and the sparsest reconstructed row found has density 2/7, capping the ratio at 21/8 = 2.625. Conjecture: sup_R rho(free R) = 21/8, so C = 3 suffices and is optimal.
findings.scope: Golden means no 00 and no 11111, as in Rule30GoldenCoupledResearch.golden_free. Searches: all 262144 right halves supported in positions 1..18, screened at n = 120 and re-measured at n = 2000..4000; all Golden streams of the form prefix + alternating tail for prefix length up to 18 (13664 of them); one- and two-slip streams with slip positions up to 41; single slips pushed to index 79 at depth 6000; all cyclically Golden words of cycle length up to 12 as purely periodic streams. Densities are deep-window measurements on depths up to 6000; rational densities are exact per-period counts of a detected cycle.
findings.result: Observed. Theta of the two pure alternating streams has density 3/7 (ratio 7/4, the published witness) and 6/7 (ratio 7/8). One slip at index 2 gives 5/14 (ratio 21/10); at index 13 or 14, 9/28 (ratio 7/3); at index 26, 2/7 (ratio 21/8). Pushing single slips to index 79 and adding a second slip never went below 2/7. Among 474 purely periodic Golden streams with positive excess rate the maximum ratio is 1.748, attained by the cycle 01 itself; nothing purely periodic beats 7/4. The best ratio realised by an actual finite right half rather than a hand-built stream is about 2.3288 (W2 of F001); the gap to 21/8 is a gap in the search over R, not a proved bound. Unknown: whether the density of Theta f is bounded below at all.

verification.limits: Exhaustive only inside the stated ranges; everything else is a measurement. Deep-window densities to depth 6000, exact eventual periods only where a cycle of length at most 200 was detected. No solver, no Lean, no kernel replay.

findings.title: R2-07: the phase-3 members of the proved ether-and-wall trap give the DENSEST sideways row, not the sparsest
findings.claim: Rule30CriticalChargeOneCoreResearch proves altCol t = ether 3 (t+1) and builds its witness as Rule30Ether.config 3 1 6 wall. Ether column 3 is [false,true,false,true], which has period two in the phase, so ether 3 (t+3) = altCol t as well: phase 3 is the same alternating driver and the published witness uses phase 1 only. The prediction was that the 27 phase-3 members of the same proved trap family would realise a sparser sideways row, which would have made F001 provable by copying an existing kernel-checked proof with different parameters.
findings.scope: config 3 3 k ws for k = 6, 13, 20, 27 with (3+k) % 7 = 2, over all 27 wall states ws with (3, ws) in Rule30Ether.wallStates. Finite computation at n = 2800.
findings.result: Refuted, reproducibly. Phase 3 realises the opposite extreme: free stream 1010... and sideways row 1011111 repeated, density 6/7, the densest in the family, ratio 7/8 rather than anything above 7/4. All 27 phase-3 wall states give the identical ratio 0.875, and so do all four values of k. The reason is the content of F002: inside the pure-ether trap, column 1 is forced to be ether column 4, so the free stream is forced to be exactly alternating, and an exactly alternating stream carries no transient.

verification.limits: n = 2800, exact integer arithmetic. No kernel replay.

findings.title: R2-02: two-sided coupled windows show no seed-orbit signature in Rule 30
findings.claim: A classifier on 5-column x 8-step two-sided windows can distinguish the single-seed Rule 30 orbit from orbits of random finite rows at held-out times.
findings.scope: Physical frame, columns -2..2, t in [64,4088), 20+20 disjoint random 33-cell rows, logistic and boosted trees, shuffled-label control; rules 30, 90, 150.
findings.result: Rule 30 held-out accuracy 0.499/0.492 (chance). Rule 150 positive control 0.996/0.999. Rule 90 degenerate (near-white).

findings.title: R2-02: the seed's column 1 is not more predictable from columns 0/1 than a generic orbit's
findings.claim: The seed's c1(t+1) is more predictable from c0[t-11..t+1], c1[t-11..t] than in generic orbits, indicating a seed-specific inheritance mechanism.
findings.scope: Target leakage excluded (c0(t+2) omitted). Train t in [76,2048), test [2048,4094); generic baseline from disjoint random orbits at matched training size 1972; rules 30, 90, 150.
findings.result: Rule 30 boosted accuracy 0.876 seed vs 0.895 generic: no seed-specific excess. Rule 150 seed 0.959 vs generic 0.514 (positive control). Rule 90 degenerate.

findings.title: R2-02: columns 0 and 1 cannot be jointly eventually periodic; Problem 1 reduces to column-1 inheritance
findings.claim: For Rule 30 from the single seed there are no T>=0, P>0 with columns 0 and 1 both P-periodic from T. Hence Problem 1 follows from: column 0 eventually periodic implies column 1 eventually periodic.
findings.scope: Exact seed, physical frame. Paper proof via left-permutivity, the light cone and the always-black left edge. Not kernel checked; likely already known.
findings.result: Paper proof in REPORT.md. The left-permutive identity checked exactly on the seed for 126 columns x 600 steps: 0 mismatches.
